name: Tessera Corponation Lattice Whisper Node
description:
The Lattice Whisper Node is a self-organizing mesh repeater designed to be deployed in clusters, with each unit autonomously discovering, authenticating, and routing through its nearest neighbors to form a decentralized communication backbone that requires no fixed infrastructure. A single Node is functionally useless; a cluster of five or more creates a resilient, self-healing network that can span several city blocks, reroute around destroyed or jammed units, and sustain encrypted voice and data traffic without any connection to GLMZ's licensed mesh infrastructure. Each unit is roughly cylindrical, about the size of a thumb, and is designed to be adhered to surfaces — undersides of benches, drainage grates, the backs of signage — where it can draw parasitic power from ambient electromagnetic fields and remain active for weeks without a dedicated power source.

The Node's defining technical feature is its adaptive routing intelligence. Rather than using fixed relay paths, the cluster continuously recalculates the most signal-efficient route through its members in response to interference, unit loss, or new additions. A Node that is physically destroyed simply drops out of the network's topology within seconds, and surrounding units redistribute the load. New Nodes introduced to an existing cluster are authenticated via a shared lattice key loaded at deployment, after which they are incorporated automatically. This makes the system highly resistant to targeted disruption — eliminating one Node accomplishes almost nothing.

Tessera Corponation markets the Lattice Whisper Node to corporate security teams for 'temporary infrastructure deployment in low-coverage operational environments,' and it is genuinely used for this purpose. It is also, with near-equal frequency, used by resistance cells, labor organizers, and underground networks to establish communications infrastructure in districts where the licensed mesh is monitored, degraded, or deliberately throttled by municipal authorities.

specifications.power_source: Ambient EM harvesting; optional micro-cell supplement for low-field environments
specifications.range_per_hop: Up to 180m in open conditions; 60–90m through dense construction
specifications.network_capacity: Up to 64 simultaneous authenticated users per 20-node cluster
specifications.operational_lifespan: 14–21 days continuous on EM harvesting alone

tactical_use: A standard deployment involves seeding 8–12 Nodes across a target area in advance of an operation, typically during a reconnaissance pass. Nodes are placed at irregular intervals and heights to maximize coverage and minimize the chance of a single sweep clearing the entire network. Once active, the cluster provides a private encrypted mesh for the operational team that is entirely independent of monitored infrastructure. The cluster can be extended in real time by introducing additional Nodes, making it possible to 'grow' the network ahead of a moving team. For extraction or exfiltration scenarios, pre-staged Nodes along a route allow continuous communication without relying on any surface that could be monitored.
cultural_context: The Lattice Whisper Node occupies a complicated legal position in GLMZ. Licensed deployment requires registration of the lattice key with the Municipal Spectrum Authority, theoretically giving authorities access to the network's traffic. In practice, the registration process is slow, inconsistently enforced, and trivially circumvented by generating new lattice keys on unlicensed hardware. This gap between legal requirement and enforcement reality has made the Node a foundational tool for everyone from legitimate corporate security teams to the city's most organized underground networks. Labor organizers in particular have adopted the technology extensively, using pre-staged clusters to maintain communication during actions in districts where municipal mesh throttling is used as a tool of crowd management.
story_hooks: A cluster of Nodes is discovered in a sealed subsection of a Tessera Corponation facility — deployed from the inside, using a lattice key that does not match any registered deployment. Someone inside the company has been running a private network for an unknown period.

Municipal authorities announce a new detection protocol targeting unregistered Whisper Node clusters, but the announcement itself is transmitted over an unregistered cluster — suggesting the leak came from inside the Spectrum Authority.

A player's pre-staged cluster goes active and begins routing traffic that was not generated by their team, suggesting either that someone else has the lattice key or that a compromised Node was introduced into their deployment.

A decommissioned Whisper Node cluster in a demolished district is still active — somehow still harvesting enough power from the rubble to maintain a partial network, and still carrying fragments of encrypted traffic from an operation that ended two years ago.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact cylindrical repeater node resembling a truncated industrial capsule or thick pen barrel, with a slightly tapered end designed for adhesive mounting. The form factor is deliberately inconspicuous—engineered to blend into urban infrastructure.
physical_description.weight_description: Lightweight and pocketable at 18g per unit; deployable in clusters without significant carrying burden
physical_description.primary_material: Brushed matte polymer composite housing with embedded EM harvesting mesh beneath surface layer
physical_description.finish: Textured, non-reflective matte gunmetal grey with subtle iridescent EM-reactive circuitry visible beneath semi-translucent polymer sections
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal grey primary body; accent bands of deep copper/bronze along ridged grip zones and ports; minimal contrast to avoid visual detection
physical_description.interface_elements: Micro-USB port recessed at tapered end for optional power supplementation; trio of micro-status LEDs (signal, mesh-sync, power harvest) embedded flush in housing; no external buttons or mechanical switches—all configuration via wireless lattice handshake
distinctive_features: Hexagonal grip ridges running the length of the cylinder for secure adhesive application and handling
Semi-translucent polymer window revealing faint lattice circuit pattern beneath surface
Integrated adhesive pad (non-permanent, repositionable) at tapered terminus
Barely-visible etched lattice symbol (Φ-derived mesh glyph) on housing
Warm amber/copper status LEDs that pulse softly when part of active cluster
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TESSERA CORPONATION logo (stylized tessellating geometric mark) on body; tiny regulatory stamp; no serial number visible (deliberately anonymized for black-market deployment)
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units appear weathered within days—dust, particulate accumulation on adhesive end, fingerprint smudges from repeated repositioning; status LEDs dim and pulse irregularly as EM harvesting fluctuates with environment; clusters deployed in industrial/urban zones often show adhesive residue or soot marking
